units.title: Carrow Point readings, day 7.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 07:00 readings: pressure 1024.6 hPa and steady, air 8.1 C, dew point 7.9 C, visibility 90 m (I cannot see my own gate), wind calm. Textbook advection fog: mild moist air sliding over cold water with nothing to stir it. The Met Office says it clears on day 9. For once I agree with them.

units.title: Recycling missed again (Rope Walk).
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: The council's notice this morning says Rope Walk recycling is 'running up to one day late' because of the fog. It was missed last week as well, in clear weather, and the week before that. I have the newsletters on my sideboard in date order if anyone at the council would like to borrow them. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: Fog delays, day 7.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: 06:40 ran, slowly. We arrived 34 minutes late, which the tannoy described as 'a little behind'. The coffee machine works. The man next to me timed the fog horn intervals out loud for the whole crossing. If it is foggy again tomorrow, I am asking nicely: nobody bring a stopwatch.

units.title: Why do Gilliver houses keep a lamp in the window?
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Odd question from the 06:40. Coming past Gilliver in the fog this morning I counted lamps lit in at least a dozen front windows at ten to seven, in what passes for daylight. Is it a fog thing? A power cut thing? My old teacher would know, but I thought I would ask you lot first.

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Same in Weyhaven, Bernard. They blame the lift, they blame the weather, they blame the lorry, they blame the residents for putting the wrong lid down. Forty years I drove the 14 through Weyhaven and I never once blamed the bus. The bus did not get a vote.

units.title: What is the Holm actually for?
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Kids at school say the Holm is going to be either a data centre, a hotel for millionaires or a bunker for when it all goes wrong. My middle one wants to know if there will be a waterslide. Does anybody actually know anything, or is it just a very big tree job? Asking for three people under twelve.

units.title: Holm planning notice lists an 'evacuation site'?
units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Just asking questions here. Someone sent me a screenshot of the Kittering Holm planning notice and the description line reads 'total vegetation clearance to facilitate a designated evacuation site'. That is not what the Courier printed today. Why would that part be left out? Who is being evacuated, and from what? Screenshot attached. Do your own research before you laugh.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: For anyone wondering why we are slow. In restricted visibility we drop to a speed at which we can stop within the distance we can see, sound the horn at intervals of not more than two minutes, and keep a dedicated lookout as well as the radar. It is slow because it is safe. Logged the delays, carried on.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Hello. It is not a fog thing. In Gilliver a good many of us keep a lamp in the front window at night, so they know the house is awake. My mother kept hers lit every night of her life and I keep mine. It is only manners, my dear. Some leave them burning into the morrning when the fog is in, because it is hard to tell when night has finished.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 1: the intermediary that bought the Holm, which I posted about earlier this week, has no history of public works or emergency planning. Finding 2: that does not make it an evacuation site. Gil, I would want the portal link, not a screenshot. A screenshot can say anything you type into it.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding: Ardent Vale's registered address is a service office in Halvard shared with around forty other companies. That is normal for holding companies and tells us nothing about what they want the island for. It tells us nothing about a waterslide either, I am sorry to report to your middle one.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Thank you for posting. Could you please give the source of the screenshot, ideally the planning portal page it was taken from and the date you saw it? Until we know where it came from I would ask everyone not to share the image elsewhere. Pell, Sound Board admin.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Heard from a lad at the plant yard its a luxury retreat, helipad and all, guests flown in from halvard. Also heard grieve are paying well but you cant leave till the jobs done. Either way if they want a subcontractor with all tickets, CS30 CS31 CS38, own kit, I am available. No job too small or too far out.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater junction lights now 'extended until day 14' according to the council. Four minute cycle confirmed, I timed it twice in the fog, once each way. Sat there long enough this evening to give the cones names. The one with the dent is Gordon. Gordon has seen things.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: I don't know where it came from originally, it was sent to me by a subscriber. I'm not saying it is real. I'm saying ask why it exists at all. The council has had two days to deny it and has said nothing. Silence is an answer too, if you know how to read it.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Thank you, that is a lovely answer. Who are 'they', though? Boats coming in? The neighbours? Sorry, I am nosy. It comes from sitting on a ferry two hours a day staring at other people's windows. Mrs Hale would tell me off for the question and for the grammar.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Thank you, skipper, that genuinely helps. I will now sit quietly and resent the fog instead of the crew. I would still like to know why the horn is reliable every two minutes and the coffee machine only works every second day, but I accept that is not your department.

units.title: Pebble update: still missing, day 7
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Still no Pebble. She is grey with one white sock, front left, and a pink collar she hates. Someone on Mill Lane thought they heard a cat crying in the fog last night, but it turned out to be a gull on a skylight. Thank you to everyone who has checked their sheds, especially Mr Arkle, who checked twice.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: It's for cutting, by the look of it. Saw their boat go over this morning with the fog sat on it like a lid. Whatever they want it for after, there's no harbour to speak of. The Holm side is all rock and weed and a landing you'd not put a hotel guest on. Aye, not a waterslide either.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: It has not had two days. It has had one afternoon, and nobody has asked it. I read that application on the portal on day 2. The description was 'total vegetation clearance, Kittering Holm' with standard conditions on nesting birds and spoil. Nothing else. I will put the portal text and the screenshot side by side tomorrow morning.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aunt Maud's right, it's manners. Some say it's for the boats coming in. Some say it's for whoever's out on the road. My grandad said it was for nobody in particular and to stop asking daft questions at the table. I keep one in the wheelhouse window too, out of habit more than anything.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: There has been no application for buildings, a grid connection, a harbour, a helipad or a change of use. Clearance consent is the only thing on file. Any of the rest would need a full application with a public consultation, and I would have read it before breakfast. That does not tell us their plans, only that none have been filed.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: I have moved this to Lost & Found, where it will be seen by the people who check that board every evening. I do hope Pebble turns up soon. If anyone has outbuildings near Mill Lane that have been shut since the fog came in, it would be kind to look.

units.title: People in Brackwater Woods at night.
units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: To whoever has been parking by the reservoir gate after dark with recording gear. The gates are locked at dusk for a reason. The banks are steep, the east ride is unlit and the deer are moving. If you hear knocking, it is two stags having an argument. Go home and listen to them from your bed.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Evening readings: 1025.1 hPa, air 7.6 C, dew point 7.6 C, so fully saturated. Visibility down to 60 m. The fog signal has been going since before breakfast and my wife has started referring to it as 'the neighbour'. Forecast for tomorrow: more neighbour.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: My eldest showed me this at tea and asked whether we would have to move. I said no, and then realised I didn't actually know what I was saying no to. Could someone sensible please confirm it is rubbish by tomorrow, so I can tell her at breakfast and get on with finding a clean PE kit?

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Have you tried shaking the biscuit box at the back door last thing at night? Our tabby came home after nine days for that sound alone, thin and furious. Also worth asking neighbours to check garages, they get shut in when people bring the bins in.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Thank you, I will try the biscuit box tonight, and the garages tomorrow. And thank you Mr Pell for moving it again. Sorry, I keep posting in General because that is where the people are. Pebble would like it noted she is not 'lost', she is 'away'.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: grow up. it's a tree job. somebody has fiddled a picture on their phone and you've fallen for it in one go. next week it'll be a launch pad. lads, it's trees.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Thank you to everyone keeping an open mind tonight. Bookmarking this thread for the day the 'sensible people' have to explain it to their kids. I'm not the one who put that line in the notice. I'm only the one who noticed.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Or it's a private refuge for the very rich and they don't need to file anything because they already own the people who read the filings. Just asking. A cleared island with no neighbours and one landing. Think about who wants that.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: That is probably me, and apologies. I park on the verge, not across the gate, and stay on the public footpath along the east ride. I will make sure I am out of everyone's way. On the deer: the knocks I've recorded are single, evenly spaced, and at 02:40, and stags don't usually clash at that hour in this month. Make of it what you will.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Some of us have been saying for a while that the Holm was never about trees... I won't say more on an open forum. Ask yourselves why it went through without a single objection. Ask who was told and who wasn't.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: There is a line in an old novel I love about a house 'keeping its eye open for those still out'. I always assumed the author had invented it. How lovely to find it is a real custom twenty miles from my shop, kept by real people. Thank you, Maud, if I may.

units.title: fog again
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: fog again lads. sound lines says the 06:40 runs slow. coastguard wants small boats in. chandlery open as usual. rope is half price today if you are the lad from Lisle whose rowing boat went for a wander

units.title: marine diesel price
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: pump price for marine diesel up 3 cents a litre from today. not my doing, its the supplier. tank is full so nobody has an excuse to run dry when the fog lifts

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Reminder to all berth holders: please check mooring lines and fenders while boats are sitting idle. Several warps on the north pontoon are chafed through to the core. Byelaw 14 requires vessels to be kept securely moored at all times. Thank you, and thank you to everyone staying in until it clears.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: From the engine room: radar fine, horn compressor fine, lookout cold. The only thing failing on board is the galley kettle, which has tripped its breaker four times today. It's an old element on a new circuit. Fixing it before anyone mutinies, because a crew in fog without tea is a safety issue.

units.title: the Gilliver slipway, for the people asking
units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: For the people asking on the boat. Night of day 4, fog, 23:50 approach. Someone standing at the very end of the Gilliver slipway where the water starts. Tall, too tall for a kid. Dark coat, no light, no torch. I hailed twice on the loud-hailer. No answer and no movement. The skipper logged it as a trespasser. That's all there is.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: fog horn every two minutes for six hours and I've started hearing it when I shut my eyes, kerris says that means I'm a real sailor now, I think it means I need earplugs, anyway if anybody has spare ones the evening crew would be very grateful and so would my mum who I am apparently honking at in my sleep

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: in fairness kerris has told this exactly the same way about nine times now including the coat and the bit about the water starting, my theory remains that it was a heron with ambitions, or the harbourmaster checking we were awake

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: A heron doesn't stand near two metres tall, Finn, and the harbourmaster answers when you hail her. I'm telling it the same way every time because that's how it was. If I start adding bits, that's when you should worry.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: earplugs in stock finn. foam ones, a box of fifty. do not wear them on deck or the skipper will have both of us

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: lads this is harbour chat. if you want to talk slipway ghosts take it to the sound board. if it's trespass on the slip thats the harbourmasters business and she will post a notice if there is one. kerris you've said your piece and nobody here thinks you're daft

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Stayed in again. Fifth day down for some of my pots. Went out to the mouth this afternoon when it thinned and turned round at the perch, couldn't see the end of my own bow. They'll be full of crabs with no claws by the time we lift them. Aye, well.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Three cents more for diesel nobody's burning. Grand. I'll fill up the day it lifts like everyone else and we can all stand in the queue at your pump and complain to your face, Rook.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: wait what slipway lol. the one by the chippy? people stand on it all the time, its the only place in gilliver you get two bars of signal. maybe it was someone on the phone to their nan
